summary: Sanders County Siegel Mountain tower, a 50-foot L-4 dated 1936 in the Lolo NF; destroyed 1965 per firelookout.com; FFLA lists it gone. No staffing or site-today source.

facts.status_note: destroyed 1965 per firelookout.com; FFLA lists it as a tower that is gone

events.note: firelookout.com dates the 50-foot L-4 tower to 1936; the Missoulian reported the station under construction in October 1936
firelookout.com says destroyed 1965; no cause given

evidence.supports: October 1936 construction of a lookout station by Forest Service men aided by CCC crews
evidence.quote: Forest service men, aided by CCC boys, are engaged in building a lookout station on Seigle peak, according to reports of one of the men employed on the work.

evidence.supports: the station would take in the Paradise area
evidence.quote: The station will include Paradise in its surveying territory.

evidence.supports: FFLA lists the tower as gone

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Siegel (firelookout.com and FFLA) and Seigle (the 1936 newspaper) are spellings of the same peak.

notes_for_editor: History rests on two pages, and the cause of the 1965 destruction is not given. The FFLA coordinates (47.29651, -114.73576) lie about 7 miles SSE of Paradise by Wikipedia's published Paradise coordinates, which I used only for this check, so they agree with the firelookout.com description. No staffing source was found. No source describes what remains at the site or whether the public can reach it.
